title: Minimum Neural Weight Norm = Kolmogorov Complexity
abstract: arXiv:2605.10878v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Why do neural networks generalize better when their parameter norm is small? We prove that, in looped neural networks with constant-precision weights, the smallest weight norm of a network computing a function is asymptotically equivalent to the Kolmogorov complexity of that function, divided by its logarithm. The proof has two reductions: looped neural networks can encode information at a rate of logarithmically many bits per non-zero parameter encoded via the sparsity pattern, while any fixed-precision network can be described by enumerating its non-zero parameters with logarithmic addressing cost. Both bounds have the same leading constant factors, giving an asymptotic equivalence. More broadly, by establishing a theoretical link between norm minimization and algorithmic simplicity, we provide an avenue towards understanding generalization in modern deep learning.

translated_title: 最小神经网络权重范数 = 柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度
translated_abstract: 为什么神经网络在参数范数较小时泛化能力更好？我们证明，在具有常数精度权重的循环神经网络中，计算某个函数的网络所需的最小权重范数与该函数的柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度除以其对数在渐近意义上等价。该证明包含两个归约：一方面，循环神经网络可以通过稀疏模式以每个非零参数编码对数级比特的速率编码信息；另一方面，任何固定精度网络都可以通过枚举其非零参数并以对数级寻址成本来描述。两个界的首项常数因子相同，从而给出了渐近等价性。更广泛地说，通过在范数最小化与算法简单性之间建立理论联系，我们为理解现代深度学习中的泛化问题提供了一条新途径。
tldr: 该论文证明了循环神经网络计算某函数所需的最小权重范数与该函数的柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度除以其对数渐近等价，从而在权重范数最小化与算法简单性之间建立了理论联系，为解释神经网络的泛化能力提供了新途径。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that the minimum weight norm of a looped neural network computing a function is asymptotically equivalent to that function's Kolmogorov complexity divided by its logarithm, establishing a theoretical link between norm minimization and algorithmic simplicity that offers a new avenue for understanding generalization in deep learning.
